title: When the Ember Sings Anew
premise: Jonah Iversen, a mercenary bound by an oath to a god who stopped answering years ago, has spent his whole life in the Ember Valley, the one place where magic cannot follow. When a mute child arrives at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Jonah and the child are dragged beyond the valley's edge into a realm where a king is being slowly consumed by the ancient thing fused to his crown — the same god that abandoned Jonah. To save both king and child, Jonah must break his oath, unbind the crown-thing in its own tongue, and choose between restoring the god's power or ending it forever; he chooses to end it, freeing the king, losing his magic-sworn strength, and finding belonging not in divine service but in the family he builds with the child.
about_author: Rafael Zhou is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent a decade documenting dying languages before turning to fantasy. They write about oaths, translation, and the violence of institutions from a small apartment full of dead dictionaries.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Establishes daily life: Jonah takes a last mercenary contract inside the valley, tends the shrine of his silent god, and drinks with folk who know him as reliable but rootless. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. On a storm night, a child of perhaps eight arrives barefoot, unafraid, speaking a language no one in the valley knows — yet Jonah half-understands it, words surfacing from his oath-training. Emotional beat: unease blooming into reluctant protectiveness.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah consults the valley's blind archivist, who identifies fragments of the speech as First-Tongue, the language of binding. The archivist warns that speakers of it are hunted. Emotional beat: dread; the child is not lost but fleeing.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridge
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Crown soldiers cross into the valley — impossible, since magic cannot follow them either — demanding the child. Jonah refuses, and for the first time feels his oath stir with borrowed heat. Emotional beat: defiance hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Oath That Answers
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Fleeing the valley at night, Jonah discovers his silent god answers through the child, who can channel the oath's power. He realizes the god never left; it was caged. Emotional beat: betrayal and awe tangled together.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Ember
chapters.summary: POV the child, Wren. Through Wren's eyes we see Jonah as a frightening, kind giant, and learn fragments of Wren's flight from the capital's Tower of Tongues. Emotional beat: cautious trust forming between two orphans of different kinds.

chapters.title: The City of Brass Bells
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. They reach the free city of Vell, seeking a translator. Jonah witnesses lawful injustice — a magistrate selling 'unbound' children to the crown — and learns justice outside the law has a price. Emotional beat: disillusionment with institutions.

chapters.title: The Translator's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A disgraced linguist, Sefa, agrees to teach them First-Tongue in exchange for Jonah breaking her out of debt-bondage. First lessons reveal the language reshapes reality when spoken truly. Emotional beat: wary alliance; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa's research reveals the crown-thing: a god-eater called the Hollow Chorus, which devoured gods one by one and now wears King Aldric like a glove. Jonah's god is its prisoner. Emotional beat: horror at scale; personal stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Lessons in Binding
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren's training montage: First-Tongue comes naturally to her because she was bred in the Tower as a vessel. She hides how much she understands about her own purpose. Emotional beat: fear of being a tool, longing to be a person.

chapters.title: The King's Procession
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The royal procession enters Vell; Jonah sees King Aldric up close and catches a flicker of the man still fighting inside. A near-catastrophic recognition scene forces them underground. Emotional beat: pity for the enemy; ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Beneath the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Hiding in Vell's undercity, the trio finds a cell of oath-breakers — mercenaries whose gods also went silent — led by a woman Jonah once fought beside. Emotional beat: belonging offered, distrusted, tentatively accepted.

chapters.title: The Price of the Broken Oath
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The oath-breakers explain: breaking his vow will strip Jonah of everything the god gave him, possibly his memories of the valley. He begins preparing anyway. Emotional beat: grief in advance; resolve kindling.

chapters.title: Wren Is Taken
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Crown agents seize Wren using a resonance trap built from her own Tower records. Jonah's rescue fails; he is left bleeding as the procession departs. Emotional beat: despair, guilt, and the cold clarity of what matters.

chapters.title: The Road to the Capital
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah, Sefa, and two oath-breakers race to the capital ahead of the coronation renewal rite, where the Hollow Chorus will finish consuming Aldric and use Wren as its new mouth. Emotional beat: grim momentum; found family forged on the road.

chapters.title: The Tower of Tongues
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Infiltrating the Tower where Wren was raised, Sefa confronts her old mentor and uncovers the final binding-word — one only a willing speaker can say. Emotional beat: reckoning with complicity; sacrifice foreshadowed.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Stone
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In the capital's crypts they reach the imprisoned god, who offers Jonah restoration if he frees it instead of destroying the Chorus. Jonah must refuse the thing he has prayed to for twenty years. Emotional beat: the book's moral crux — power refused.

chapters.title: Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Wren. At the renewal rite, Wren, forced to speak the Chorus's opening words, instead slips true bindings into the liturgy, buying seconds. Jonah breaches the hall. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into courage; the child saves herself first.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Climax: Jonah breaks his oath aloud in First-Tongue, shattering his own power to crack the crown's hold, while Sefa speaks the unbinding at cost of her voice. The Hollow Chorus is unraveled; Aldric wakes screaming. Emotional beat: triumphant devastation.

chapters.title: What the King Owes
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Freed Aldric must face what he did while crowned; Jonah refuses a reward and instead demands the Tower of Tongues be dissolved and the children freed. Justice outside the law becomes law reluctantly bent. Emotional beat: weary vindication.

chapters.title: The Silence After Gods
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Aftermath: the freed god, diminished and mortal-bound, asks Jonah to serve it anew; he declines, choosing the human bonds he made. Sefa, voiceless, finds new ways to speak. Emotional beat: mourning what was lost, honoring what was chosen.

chapters.title: When the Ember Sings Anew
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Jonah returns to the valley with Wren and Sefa, planting a garden over the empty shrine. Wren speaks First-Tongue to the hearthfire, and for the first time in years, something warm and small answers. Emotional beat: homecoming; belonging earned, not sworn.
